html:
1. Understanding Delaware’s Home Health Market

Home health agencies in Delaware operate under the regulatory authority of the Delaware Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS), through its Division of Health Care Quality. The market presents moderate opportunity for new providers, driven by an aging population and Medicaid HCBS waivers.

Key Market Indicators:

  • Services are concentrated along Delaware’s I-95 corridor and major population hubs
  • Rural Sussex County and Kent County have fewer providers and lower capacity
  • Medicaid long-term services prioritize clients through managed care
  • Related housing services linked to home care report average waits of 3 years and 10 months

Reimbursement Environment:

  • Home Health Agency (HHA) Medicaid rate: approximately $36.56/hour
  • Personal Assistance Services Agency (PASA) rate: approximately $27.42/hour
  • Medicare home health reimbursements reflect a nationwide 2.2% decrease for 2024

2. Licensing Requirements

Licensing is governed by Delaware Administrative Code Title 16, Chapter 3350.

Application Process:

  • Submit licensing application to DHSS Division of Health Care Quality
  • Administrator and key personnel background checks
  • Demonstration of financial viability
  • Policies and procedures manual submission
  • Quality assurance program documentation
  • Compliance with staffing qualifications

Medicare/Medicaid Certification:

  • Separate certification process beyond state licensing
  • Survey and accreditation requirements
  • Quality reporting obligations
  • Conditions of Participation compliance

3. Business Structure and Registration

Required Steps:

  • Register with Delaware Division of Corporations
  • Obtain Delaware business license
  • Apply for federal EIN
  • NPI (National Provider Identifier) registration
  • State Medicaid provider enrollment
  • Medicare provider enrollment (if applicable)

Insurance Requirements:

  • Professional liability (malpractice) insurance
  • General liability insurance
  • Workers’ compensation
  • Bonding (may be required)
  • Vehicle insurance for staff travel

4. Financial Planning

Revenue Projections:

  • Agencies operating at 70-80% capacity may expect 10-15% gross margins
  • Break-even timeline: 12-24 months
  • Workforce shortages significantly impact timeline
  • Payer mix optimization is critical for profitability

Startup Costs:

  • Office space and setup: $20,000 – $75,000
  • Licensing and certification fees: $5,000 – $15,000
  • Initial staffing and recruitment: $50,000 – $150,000
  • Technology systems (EMR, scheduling): $10,000 – $50,000
  • Working capital (6 months): $100,000 – $300,000

5. Staffing Requirements

Key Clinical Positions:

  • Registered Nurses (RNs)
  • Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs)
  • Certified Nursing Assistants (CNAs)
  • Physical Therapists
  • Occupational Therapists
  • Speech-Language Pathologists
  • Medical Social Workers

Administrative Positions:

  • Administrator/Director
  • Director of Nursing
  • Compliance Officer
  • Billing and Coding Staff
  • Scheduling Coordinator

Workforce Challenges:

  • Delaware reports approximately 500 RN and 150 LPN vacancies statewide
  • Competitive compensation packages essential for recruitment
  • Retention strategies critical in tight labor market

6. Service Delivery Models

High-Demand Niches:

  • Medicaid waiver program specialization (elderly, disabled populations)
  • Skilled nursing and therapy services bundled with home care
  • Personal assistance with integrated care coordination technologies
  • Expansion into underserved rural areas, particularly Sussex County

7. Quality and Compliance

Regulatory Compliance:

  • Adherence to Delaware Administrative Code Title 16, Chapter 3350
  • Regular DHSS inspections and surveys
  • Quality reporting to CMS (for Medicare-certified agencies)
  • Patient satisfaction measurement and improvement

Best Practices:

  • Electronic health records implementation
  • Care coordination protocols
  • Infection control programs
  • Emergency preparedness planning
  • Staff competency evaluations

8. Regulatory Contacts

  • DHSS Division of Health Care Quality: Primary licensing authority
  • Division of Medicaid and Medical Assistance: Medicaid enrollment
  • CMS Regional Office: Medicare certification
  • Delaware Division of Corporations: Business entity registration
